Sandpapergate: Former Australia head coach Darren Lehmann denies knowledge of sandpaper use after Cameron Bancroft allegations
Former Australia head coach Darren Lehmann has denied knowledge of the use of sandpaper, directly contradicting Cameron Bancroft's claims that the coaching staff were aware of the plot to tamper with the ball; Bancroft named Lehmann as present in the discussions around sandpaper use
Saturday 21 November 2026 08:39, UK
Former Australia head coach Darren Lehmann has denied knowledge of the use of sandpaper to alter the ball during his side's Test series against South Africa in 2018.
The development comes after batter Cameron Bancroft - who was caught on camera using sandpaper - exacerbated the Sandpapergate scandal with a 4,000-word statement asserting that the entire team - including the bowling group - knew about the use of sandpaper on the three-Test tour of South Africa in 2018.
Bancroft named Lehmann as one of the members present in a discussion around the use of sandpaper, even quoting his former coach in directing an assistant to take the sandpaper from Bancroft once the ball-tampering had been discovered by the TV broadcast.

- Sandpapergate: News and reaction to ball-tampering scandal
- Listen to latest episode of the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast
Lehmann has now denied those claims, telling BBC's Test Match Special: "No. I didn't know sandpaper was being used.
"I was coach at the time, I've got to take that responsibility.
"It was the best job in the world. I'm sorry for what happened."
"It's my fault it went too far."
The recollection of Lehmann, now Northamptonshire head coach, directly contradicts that of Bancroft, who was unequivocal in his belief that Lehmann was aware of the team's plot to tamper with the ball.
"Boof [Lehmann's nickname] shouted on the walkie talkie 'get the f***ing sandpaper off Bangers now'," Bancroft wrote in his statement on Wednesday.
"In my opinion, if he didn't know he wouldn't have said that. And if it wasn't clear enough before, then it was obvious now. Once again. WE ALL KNEW."
The decision adds to a furore of discussion around the 2018 scandal, with former Australian opener Usman Khawaja's book first bringing to light claims the entire team knew about the use of sandpaper.
Khawaja also alleged discussions about ball-tampering had been held "openly and lightheartedly" across the entire squad, involving not just the batters, bowlers and coaching staff but the wider team.
Those claims align with Bancroft's new statement, and with the recollection of former seamer Chadd Sayers, who also asserted that "everyone in that [2018] side" was aware of the ball-tampering taking place on the tour.
Backing for Cummins, Hazlewood criticises 'pile on'
Cummins, who earlier on Saturday received "unanimous support" from Cricket Australia to continue as Test and ODI captain, called Khawaja's claims "complete and utter nonsense" during a sensational 68-minute press conference on Friday of last week.
He was also backed up by fellow fast bowler Josh Hazlewood, who criticised the "pile on" against Cummins, saying he would consider his position in the Test side if he was forced to stand down as captain.
Hazlewood's comments followed those of another bowler in Mitchell Starc, who earlier this month also claimed "his recollection hadn't changed since 2021" when the bowlers released a joint statement denying knowledge.
Bancroft's detailed claims also came in the wake of Cricket Australia announcing an independent forum to explore the scandal. It stated players could share their version of events without fears of reprisals.

מאמן נבחרת אוסטרליה לשעבר, דרק לימן, הכחיש באופן גורף כל ידיעה מוקדמת על השימוש בנייר שחזת כדי לשנות את מצב הכדור במהלך סדרת הטסט נגד דרום אפריקה ב-2018. הכחשתו מגיעה בעקבות הצהרה מפורטת של שחקן הנבחרת לשעבר, קמרון בנקרופט, שבה טען כי צוות האימון, ולימן בתוכו, היה מודע היטב למתרחש ואף נכח בדיונים על אודות הפעולה האסורה.

למרות עדויות נוספות מצד אנשי צוות ושחקנים לשעבר שטענו כי כל חברי הסגל והצוות ידעו על המעשה, לימן עמד על שלו בריאיון ל-BBC וציין כי לא ידע על כך דבר, הגם שלקח אחריות כוללת על כך שהדברים הלכו רחוק מדי בתקופתו כמאמן ראשי. במקביל, קפטן הנבחרת פט קאמינס זכה לתמיכה מלאה מאיגוד הקריקט האוסטרלי לאחר שדחה טענות דומות שהועלו בספרו של אוסמאן חוואג'ה, בעוד ששחקנים נוספים גיבו את עמדתו ויצאו נגד הביקורת הציבורית המוגברת.
